rationale: Presented six JoinKind values as the full set; JoinKind.Type documents eight (adds LeftSemi, RightSemi).
Said the toggle lives under Settings > Upcoming features; docs say on by default for new apps, and Settings > Updates > New for existing apps.
Comment claimed defaults are effectively unbounded; only resolveTimeout is infinite (connect 60s, send 30s, receive 30s). Advice to set all four survives; rationale replaced with the argument order.
Listed First as categorically non-delegable; MS Learn names First among delegable filter functions. Corrected in power-fx-review and delegation.md; FirstN/Last/LastN remain non-delegable.
Listed roles as read/write/fullcontrol/owner; docs list read/write/manage/fullcontrol. 'Owner' is a Sites.Selected tier, not a grantable role value.
Claimed app-only AND Sites.Selected both require admin consent; the permissions reference marks delegated Sites.Selected AdminConsentRequired: No. Scoped the claim to Application permissions.
Stated as required-or-HTTP-400 across five locations; absent from the official listItem:list reference. Reproduced widely in the field but community-sourced — labeled rather than deleted.
exactin is doc-stated non-delegable everywhere; 'in' is only ABSENT from SharePoint's delegable-operations table. Omission means unconfirmed, not unsupported — kept the guidance, labeled the basis.
The IsBlank -> = Blank() rewrite is doc-stated; the simple-vs-Person/Lookup/Choice restriction is a field extension the docs neither state nor contradict.

Community lore that Learn actively pushes against (both kinds computed at refresh and stored; calculated columns can win for some aggregations). Rationale replaced with a defensible one and the lore flagged.
Docs list only 0/1/TRUE/FALSE for the order argument; DESC/ASC are widely accepted in practice but undocumented.
RELATED's row-context requirement is doc-stated; RELATEDTABLE's page describes it only as CALCULATETABLE with no filter and states no such requirement.
That removal list is documented for the Rich text editor control, not for HtmlText. Behaviour is real in practice; the citation was misattributed.
Function input kinds are documented; the verbatim error message is observed, not doc-stated.
Long-established VBA behaviour stated only in community answers; the no-side-effects rule is documented for JS custom functions, not VBA UDFs.
Cross-project hiding is doc-stated; hiding from the host macro dialog is a well-known effect the Learn page does not mention.
Documented on the Access TextBox KeyPress page; the MSForms KeyPress page omits it.

Code comment claimed MacroOptions throws when the Category already exists; docs state an existing category name is REUSED (and a built-in name maps to that built-in category). Guard kept, rationale fixed.

Export is documented as saving 'a separate file or files' and the Export File dialog lists only .frm/.bas/.cls; the .frx companion is real in practice but never named on current Learn (three targeted searches).
Docs describe the 'Application-defined or object-defined error' message but never tie it to number 1004; Excel raises 1004 with many message texts. Row reworded to reflect that.

id.symbol: code edit invalidates VBA project signature

rationale: Modify-invalidates is doc-stated for workbook-content signatures, not for VBA project signatures; Office may silently re-sign on save when the cert is present. Advice kept, basis labeled.

No Learn statement on expiry behaviour for VBA project signatures; a timestamped signature can survive cert expiry in general code-signing, so the blanket claim may overstate. Hedged rather than asserted.

id.symbol: add-in procedures callable with no reference

rationale: True for worksheet UDFs and Application.Run (docs: macro names need not be qualified), but calling add-in procedures from another project's VBA code does require a reference. Sentence scoped accordingly.

CONTRADICTORY FIRST-PARTY SOURCES: the current support article says SharePoint (M365) allows manually indexing a list of any size, while a live Learn troubleshooting page still states a 20,000-item limit to add/remove an index (documented for Server 2016/2019). Recorded as drift rather than resolved; conclusion (index early) unchanged.

Rests only on a community Q&A answer; the official article describes automatic index SELECTION (Metadata Navigation picks the best existing index), not automatic index CREATION. Labeled as community-sourced.
RelationshipDeleteBehaviorType (None/Cascade/Restrict) is doc-stated; the 'primary lookup columns only' and 'throttled on large lists' qualifiers were not found in any doc.
Docs support it indirectly (a UI rename creates a separate display property while list settings show the original) but never state the frozen-internal-name rule outright.

4 of 6 rows misstated the documented semantics (2 called load-on-demand when it is the post-failure error state; 8 'load next time then 2' when it becomes 9; 9 called load-at-startup when it is load-on-demand; 16 called rare when Learn names it one of three intended install values). Table rebuilt from the registry-entries reference as state-x-rule.

Same enum wrong differently in a second file: 2 described as load-on-demand and 0 as 'Office disabled it after repeated failures'. 2 is the post-failure demotion; 0 is a deliberate don't-load-automatically setting. Hard-disable surfaces via Disabled Items, a separate mechanism.

MSI-deployed add-ins require the file:/// prefix on the Manifest registry value; without it the VSTO runtime cannot resolve the deployment manifest. An MSI built from the template as written would not load.

Signed the deployment manifest first; the deployment manifest embeds a hash of the application manifest, so that order is invalidated by the later app-manifest signature. Corrected to -Update app manifest, then -Update .vsto with -AppManifest.

The ClickOnce registry example carried |vstolocal, which opts OUT of the ClickOnce cache and belongs to Windows Installer deployments — it contradicted the install/update model the same section described.

'Changing the publish URL breaks all installed clients; treat as permanent' overstates: it is recoverable via setup.exe /url=. The real constraint is the deploymentProvider codebase. Advice kept, framing fixed.
Computer-assigned packages install at computer STARTUP; user-assigned install at logon. The step described a computer-configuration package installing at next login.
The documented restriction is version-scoped (same version, different installation technologies). Different-version coexistence is supported, subject to bitness.

id.symbol: VSTO logging via EnableLogging registry value

rationale: No documented EnableLogging value under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\VSTO\Security. Startup logging is enabled with the VSTO_LOGALERTS environment variable; the log is <add-in>.vsto.log beside the deployment manifest. VSTOInstaller.log is a different tool's artifact.
A VSTO add-in is a class library in the Office host process; a component cannot select the CLR — only an application's own config can. Reframed as a targeting/prerequisite issue.
Office LTSC 2021 has NO Extended Support phase — five years of Mainstream Support ending 2026-10-13. Relabeled 'end of support'.
Receives cumulative security AND reliability/quality updates with no announced end of support; 'maintenance mode, security fixes only' overstates the freeze.

FRESHNESS FAILURE, not an authoring error: true when written, but from Version 2606 (July 2026) SAEC receives Monthly Enterprise builds and 'Monthly Channel' is no longer a channel name. Staging lever is now version pinning/rollback. Carries a check-current-policy caveat.

Framing was backwards. Learn attributes the access-violation hazard to ReleaseComObject and explicitly suggests FinalReleaseComObject when deterministic release is wanted. Reviewable defect is releasing an RCW others may hold (singletons, caller-supplied objects) — including the skill's own ItemAdd 'FIX'.
Value2 is typed object; the only difference from Value is that it never uses Currency or Date (dates arrive as OADate double). It still returns string/bool/error values.

id.symbol: background-thread OM call is an STA violation

rationale: Calls are automatically marshaled across the STA boundary; the documented failure is a rejected call surfacing as COMException (application busy / RPC_E_SERVERCALL_RETRYLATER) plus blocking. Rule restated as 'needs COMException handling with retry, or marshal to UI thread'.

ThisAddIn_Shutdown is not raised when Outlook exits (only when the user disables the add-in), so unsubscribe code there silently never runs. Outlook cleanup belongs on Application.Quit or Explorer.Close. Fixed in VSTO-development and VSTO-review.

Any CPU (the Office project default) runs under both 32-bit and 64-bit Office; bitness only matters when deliberately targeting x86/x64 for native interop. Learn says you typically should not change the setting.

id.symbol: two-dot rule / foreach enumerator leak / Outlook item recycling

rationale: The review skill's three core doctrines are long-standing VSTO practice, consistent with documented RCW behaviour, but stated outright nowhere on Learn. Kept and labeled; reviewers told not to cite a doc page for them.
Documented behaviour the skill omitted: ItemAdd does not run when many items are added at once, so designs relying on it for completeness silently miss batches. Added with the reconcile fix.

Listed as a common upgrade breakage, but parsing got MORE lenient in that window — 3.11 widened fromisoformat to most ISO 8601 including the Z suffix, and 3.12 documents no stricter-parsing change. Replaced with the real 3.12 datetime breakage (utcnow/utcfromtimestamp deprecation), which the skill already named correctly elsewhere.
Real removal but it landed in 3.13, listed under a '3.9 -> 3.12' example. Each breakage in the bullet is now tagged with the version that actually did it.
The decorator lives under .mark — bare pytest.parametrize raises AttributeError, so the instruction as written produces broken test code.

SAME CLASS AS THE VSTO-REVIEW REVERSALS: the review skill's example of the bug was actually the documented FIX. `lambda i: i` shadows the loop variable via its parameter and does not capture it; binding-by-default-argument is what Python's FAQ prescribes as the cure. A reviewer following this would flag correct code and miss the real parameterless capture. Verified empirically.

Only the CLI use is deprecated — packaging.python.org states setup.py as a setuptools CONFIG file 'is absolutely fine'. Scoped to invoking python setup.py <command>, with pyproject.toml still preferred for new metadata.

PEP 249 defines multiple paramstyles (%s for psycopg2/MySQL, ? for sqlite3); the example implied one universal symbol. Annotated as driver-specific — the parameterization is the point, not the placeholder.

Formula is correct but the i.i.d./serially-uncorrelated assumption was implicit — and sat in tension with the same skill's fat-tails-and-clustering warning. Assumption now stated in backtesting-validation and quant-code-review. An internal inconsistency the gate surfaced, not a factual error.

'annual return / max drawdown' matches modern general usage, but Young's canonical 1991 definition pins a trailing 36-month window and a compound (CAGR) numerator. Labeled as the general form with the window/return convention called out.

Preferring linalg.solve to an explicit inverse is settled numerical-analysis practice but appears nowhere in the NumPy/SciPy docs, which warn only about singular/ill-conditioned input. Kept as a review item, labeled craft rather than citable rule.
